evidence.note: Keyser argues that Letter II in its current form is not Platonic, adducing dating, doctrinal, hiatus and technological evidence and proposing a later intellectual context.
Bury judges Letter II fairly certainly inauthentic, emphasizing conflicts of tone and content with the stronger Sicilian letter tradition.
Helfer (2023) revives a serious minority position that treats the thirteen Letters as a deliberately unified Platonic literary-philosophical work.

rationale: Letter II has a substantial history of defense, but the stronger modern case points against Platonic authorship. Bury regarded it as fairly certainly inauthentic, and Keyser developed a detailed chronological, doctrinal and linguistic case for a substantially later provenance. Because serious scholarship has nevertheless defended the letter, and a recent monograph again argues for a unified Platonic design of the letter collection, PROJECT PLATO classifies it as C rather than D.
